analysis_path.path_description: Run Tukey biweight robust linear regression of individual log wage gain on paper-aligned education groups, using college degree as the reference and estimating the no-high-school contrast while controlling for available country, sex, age, timing, and pre-migration sector/occupation variables.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Verify that required columns exist: edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, country, sex, yrborn, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, occGroupLastHomeJob.
Report starting row count.
Drop rows missing required raw variables and report rows removed.
Drop rows with lastHomeWageAdjusted <= 0 or lastUsWageAdjusted <= 0 and report rows removed.
Compute log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Recode edyrs into five education groups: no_high_school <= 8; some_high_school 9-11; high_school 12; some_college 13-15; college_degree >= 16.
Compute age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job squared.
Drop rows with nonfinite or missing constructed variables and report rows removed.
Estimate robust RLM with TukeyBiweight norm using college_degree as the education reference.

Report the coefficient, normal-approximation standard error, z statistic, p-value, 95% interval, exponentiated proportional difference, final analytic N, and conclusion classification for no_high_school relative to college_degree.

key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Categorical edu_group from edyrs, with no_high_school defined as edyrs <= 8 and college_degree defined as edyrs >= 16.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Authorized dataset rows with positive adjusted wages and nonmissing variables required by the adjusted robust regression.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No rows are trimmed; Tukey biweight robust regression downweights influential residuals.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw and constructed variables.
key_choices.data_processing: Log transformation of adjusted wage ratio; education-year categorization; age-at-home-job construction; categorical treatment of education, country, sex, and home occupation/sector group.
key_choices.model_choice: Tukey biweight robust linear regression using statsmodels RLM.
key_choices.inference_rule: An estimate in the expected positive direction is support; p < 0.05 is strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 is weak directional support. A negative estimate is opposite only with affirmative evidence of a material contrary effect; otherwise it is inconclusive.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference="college_degree")) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob + C(occGroupLastHomeJob)
models.planned_estimation: Robust-regression coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in log_wage_gain, plus exponentiated proportional difference exp(coef)-1.
models.inference_criteria: Support if the coefficient is positive; p < 0.05 indicates strong evidence and p >= 0.05 indicates weak directional support. A negative coefficient is opposite only if p < 0.05, otherwise inconclusive.
models.qualification: The focal outcome and contrast are preserved. Tukey biweight robust regression is a defensible robustness analysis because inspected adjusted wage variables contain extreme values, and it differs from prior OLS, median quantile, trimmed OLS, and Huber paths without choosing a method based on expected results. Task1 is unrestricted, and the available sector/occupation variable is paper-relevant because the paper summary notes prior employment sector as a determinant of wage gains.

candidates.decision_summary: Task1 passes all thirteen required checks. The original paper studies observational immigrant wage histories comparing pre- and post-migration wages for individual immigrants, and the focal paper claim is an education-gradient claim that immigrants with no high-school exposure have larger wage gains than college-degree immigrants. The authorized dataset has 2854 individual rows, the required adjusted home and U.S. wage variables, edyrs, country, sex, job-year variables, birth year, and occGroupLastHomeJob; no person ID or repeated-measure structure is present beyond the two wage observations already collapsed into one individual wage gain. The code uses only the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx file, constructs log_wage_gain from adjusted wages, categorizes edyrs into the five paper-aligned groups with college_degree as reference, and estimates the planned Tukey biweight RLM with the stated Task1 controls. It reports starting rows, missing-data exclusions, nonpositive-wage exclusions, constructed-variable exclusions, final analytic N, the focal no_high_school coefficient, standard error, p-value, confidence interval, exponentiated difference, and conclusion classification. No low-quality rule is triggered: M1/Rule 1.2 do not apply because the estimand, scale, contrast, population, and time scope match the focal claim; M2/M4 do not apply because variables, transformations, controls, and the robust outlier-handling choice are verified and justified; M3 does not apply because sample flow is reported; M5 does not apply because education categorization is required by the claim; M6/Rule 1.1 do not apply because plan and code are consistent; Rule 1.4 does not apply because an identifiable entry file and run command are present. Guardrails G1, G8, and G14 were considered: using Tukey biweight robust regression rather than the paper's exact specification is a defensible robustness choice for extreme adjusted wage values and does not by itself make the candidate low-quality.

Keep rows with nonmissing edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, and country.
Keep rows with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages.
Keep rows with finite constructed log_wage_gain and edu_group.
exclusion_rules: Drop rows missing required raw variables.
Drop rows with nonpositive adjusted wages.
Drop rows with missing or nonfinite constructed variables.
Do not control for or condition on sector or rural/urban region.

focal_variable_structure.source_structure: edyrs is continuous/integer years of education.
focal_variable_structure.analysis_structure: Categorical five-group education predictor with college_degree as reference.
focal_variable_structure.information_loss: Education years are collapsed into five groups, losing within-group variation.
focal_variable_structure.justification: The focal claim is explicitly group-based and the paper summary notes five educational groups, so categorization is required to estimate the stated contrast.

code_preflight.preflight_note: Read-back verified that the script constructs log_wage_gain and edu_group as declared, retains the full authorized sample including Mexico, adds no sector/region/control variables to the formula, uses TukeyBiweight RLM, reports sample-flow attrition, and outputs the focal no_high_school coefficient.

analysis_code.notes: Run from the study directory. The script writes results_task2.json and model_summary_task2.txt into its artifact directory.

candidates.decision_summary: Task2 passes all thirteen required checks. The Task2 instruction requires the pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects wage-gain sample including Mexico and no sector/agriculture-nonagriculture or rural/urban region controls. The authorized file contains Mexico and is documented as the required pooled sample; it has 2854 individual immigrant rows, no missing focal variables, positive adjusted wages in the inspected summaries, and no person ID indicating repeated observations. The code treats the authorized file as the full pooled sample, explicitly retains all countries including Mexico, constructs log_wage_gain from adjusted home and U.S. wages, creates the five education groups with college_degree as reference, and estimates only log_wage_gain on education groups using Tukey biweight RLM. It does not include sector, agriculture/nonagriculture, rural/urban region, country, demographic, or timing controls in the formula. It reports all material sample-flow steps and focal output. No low-quality rule is triggered: Rules 2.1, 2.2, and 2.3 do not apply because the required outcome, predictor, sample, contrast, transformation, and control prohibition are implemented; Rule 2.5 does not apply because the Task2 result is traceable to source code and an entry command; Rule 2.6 does not apply because the planned conclusion classification follows the fixed rule that a positive coefficient is support regardless of p-value strength. M1-M6 are not triggered. Guardrails G1, G8, and G14 were considered: the robust Tukey estimator is a defensible model-family deviation motivated by extreme wage values and does not add prohibited controls or change the focal estimand.

same_focal_claim.note: The candidate estimates the no-high-school versus college-degree difference in wage gains required by the focal claim and Task2.

same_dataset.note: The code reads only the authorized data/wage_gain_table.xlsx and treats it as the pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects sample including Mexico.

not_duplicate.note: Shared Memory contains unadjusted OLS, median quantile, trimmed OLS, and Huber RLM Task2 paths. This unadjusted Tukey biweight RLM path is a distinct robust M-estimator path.

estimand_alignment.note: The unadjusted coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in log adjusted wage gain aligns with Task2's quantity, scale, contrast, population including Mexico, and last-home-job to last-U.S.-job time scope.

variable_support.note: edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, and country are verified columns. The education cutoffs and log adjusted wage-gain construction are authorized by the task anchor.
